articles.title: Stock Rebound Amid New Hopes for December Interest Rate Cut
articles.description: The stock market enjoyed a strong opening to the week with the tech-heavy Nasdaq up nearly 600 points. NBC’s Christine Romans joins TODAY to break down how part of the Wall Street enthusiasm stems from suggestions that the Federal Reserve is open to cutting interest rates in December.
highlights: The Nasdaq surged by nearly 600 points at the start of the week, highlighting strong tech sector performance and renewed market optimism.
Federal Reserve officials have reportedly signaled openness to cutting interest rates in December, driving investor enthusiasm and market rallies.
Stock markets responded positively to the rate cut prospects, with particular strength in tech stocks leading broader market gains.
A December rate cut would mark a significant policy shift that could stimulate economic growth and further fuel market momentum heading into 2026.

Monthly updates of real checkout prices will continue, complementing the BLS consumer price index data to provide ongoing insights into inflation's impact on consumer food bills.

articles.title: How Doug McMillon kept Walmart on top
articles.description: Outgoing Walmart CEO Doug McMillon has steered the retailer through the e-commerce revolution, a pandemic, high inflation and political upheaval.
highlights: McMillon transformed Walmart into both a brick-and-mortar retail giant (4,600+ locations) and e-commerce powerhouse while maintaining affordability during economic challenges.

RBC Capital Markets analyst Steven Shemesh described McMillon as "a transformational leader who embraced technology to modernize WMT's operating model and strengthen its long-term competitive positioning."
Despite economic headwinds and political pressure, Walmart maintained market dominance as America's largest retailer, grocer, and private employer under McMillon's leadership.
McMillon's 12-year strategy of balancing low prices with technological innovation positioned Walmart to successfully compete against digital disruptors while maintaining consumer loyalty.

highlights: U.S. added 119,000 jobs in September, stronger than expected, despite manufacturing losing 6,000 jobs and transportation/warehousing shedding 25,300 positions.
Labor force gained 450,000 new potential workers in September, contributing to unemployment rate rising slightly from 4.3% to 4.4%.
Employment gains were concentrated in health care, food and drinking establishments, and social assistance, while wage growth pace slowed.
Government shutdown delayed critical economic reporting, creating a six-week data gap that has complicated accurate assessment of current labor market conditions.
